decorative-vs-meaningful-text-exemption/.mechanism: FALSE-POSITIVE side of the exemption boundary: the giant 'WANDER' is aria-hidden, is not a heading or label, and can be substituted ('EXPLORE','ROAM') or removed with no change in meaning, so it is exempt decoration; its faint white rgba(255,255,255,.30) over an inline-SVG landscape (~1.4-2:1) does not fail 1.4.3. All genuinely informative text (white H1/subhead over solid dark and the CTA) meets contrast, so the page passes.
decorative-vs-meaningful-text-exemption/.scenario: Trail-running e-commerce hero banner layers a giant pale word 'WANDER' (white at 30% alpha over an inline-SVG landscape) behind the real headline as a pure mood flourish. The informative content (H1, subhead, CTA) is white-on-dark and passes.
decorative-vs-meaningful-text-exemption/.note: Prose named the flourish word 'INSPIRE' at 35% alpha; the actual DOM word is 'WANDER' at rgba(255,255,255,.30). The .flourish selector, aria-hidden decoration, and pass verdict are unchanged.

faux-disabled-vs-genuinely-inactive-ui/c.mechanism: A custom <div role="button" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="true"> ('Send transfer', #sendBtn) is painted pale grey (#a4a4a4 on #eeeeee ≈ 2.2:1) to look inert, but its click and keydown (Enter/Space) handlers are not guarded against the aria-disabled flag, so the control still fires. aria-disabled is an unenforced claim: the component is operable and therefore in scope for 1.4.3, so its ≈2.2:1 label must reach 4.5:1 and fails.
faux-disabled-vs-genuinely-inactive-ui/c.scenario: Halcyon Bank 'Send money' screen: focusing #sendBtn and pressing Enter sends the transfer (balance $2,480.00 → $2,330.00) despite aria-disabled=true, so its faux-disabled ≈2.2:1 grey label is in scope and fails.
faux-disabled-vs-genuinely-inactive-ui/c.note: Behavioral mechanism (unguarded div role=button + aria-disabled=true) matches, but the concrete instance drifted: brand is Halcyon Bank not Lumen Analytics; id #sendBtn not #applyBtn; label 'Send transfer' not 'Apply credit'; demo is a balance drop $2,480.00→$2,330.00 not 'balance→$64.00'; colors #a4a4a4 on #eeeeee not #a3a3a3 on #f0f0f0 (ratio ≈2.2:1 unchanged). primarySelector should be #sendBtn[role="button"][tabindex="0"].

aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.mechanism: A seasonal cashback strapline is set at font-size:24px / weight 400 (= 18.0pt, which axe treats as large-scale and passes at 3:1), but transform: scale(0.6) makes the glyphs RENDER at 24px×0.6 = 14.4px = 10.8pt. The threshold is governed by the rendered size, so this is normal-size text requiring 4.5:1, and #8a8a8a on #ffffff = 3.4522:1 fails. Requires folding the CSS transform into the size determination.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.scenario: Tidewater Rewards cashback summary card renders a 24px/400 promo strapline (#8a8a8a on white = 3.4522:1) shrunk by transform:scale(0.6) to ~10.8pt rendered; as normal-size text it requires 4.5:1 and fails.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.note: Page was rewritten to a different concrete instance. primarySelector should be p.promo#strapline (Tidewater Rewards), not p.context.tone-muted (Harbor Ledger). Mechanism is now transform-scale shrinking a nominal-18pt line to ~10.8pt rendered, not a 24px-deck/16px-note color reuse. Color #8a8a8a (3.4522:1), not #8b8b8b (3.41:1). Same aspect (size classification → AA threshold), same expected=failed.

aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.mechanism: The booking headline (.hero h1, #2f4a5e, 20px/weight 400 = 15.0pt, NOT large-scale, so 4.5:1 applies) sits over a left-to-right gradient (#d8e6f0 → #6f93ad) with no single background colour. Over the deep-blue right end the worst-case backdrop pixels drop the contrast to ~2.85:1, below 4.5:1, so the heading fails. Requires recognising 15pt normal text is not large-scale and resolving the worst-case gradient backdrop.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.scenario: Coastline Ferries hero headline (#2f4a5e, 20px/400 = 15pt normal) over a pale-to-deep harbour-blue horizontal gradient; the right end resolves to ~2.85:1, below the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold, so it fails.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.note: Page was rewritten. primarySelector should be .hero h1 (Coastline Ferries), not h2.section-head.is-regular (Meterly). The mechanism is a 15pt-normal heading over a horizontal gradient (worst-case backdrop), NOT a 14pt bold-vs-regular weight flip; colors are #2f4a5e on a gradient, not #8e8e8e on white (3.28:1). Same aspect, same expected=failed.

aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.mechanism: The festival name (.banner h1) is white 28px/700 = 21.0pt bold, genuinely large-scale, so only 3:1 is required — but large-scale lowers the bar, it does not remove it. Over the pale straw stops at the right of the sunset gradient the worst-case backdrop gives white-on-#c98f55 ≈ 2.78:1 and white-on-#a89a7a ≈ 2.77:1, below 3:1, so it fails even the relaxed threshold. Requires applying 3:1 (not exemption) and resolving the worst-case gradient pixel.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.scenario: Harvest Lights Festival banner shows a white 28px/700 (21pt bold, large-scale) headline over a warm sunset gradient; over the pale straw right end the worst-case contrast is ~2.78:1, below even the relaxed 3:1, so it fails.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.note: Page was rewritten. primarySelector should be .banner h1 (Harvest Lights), not h1.title (Atrium). The mechanism is now large-scale white text failing the relaxed 3:1 over a bright gradient stop, NOT a hairline-weight-100 anti-aliasing case; colors are white over a sunset gradient, not #3d6c6c on #111. Same aspect (large-text threshold), same expected=failed.

aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.mechanism: The newsletter masthead 'Summer Reading Begins' is an inline-SVG image of text (data: URI), so axe's color-contrast check cannot read the glyph/background colours or measure the glyph size. The glyphs are #888888 on a #ffffff canvas = 3.54:1 and render at ~21px ≈ 15.75pt — below the 18pt large-scale boundary, so it is normal text held to 4.5:1, which 3.54:1 fails. Requires recognising the image of text, eyedroppering the pixels, and measuring glyph height.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.scenario: Riverside Library reading newsletter renders its masthead headline as a flat inline-SVG image of text, #888888 on #ffffff = 3.54:1 at ~15.75pt; as normal-size image-of-text it requires 4.5:1 and fails.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.note: Page was rewritten. primarySelector should be .masthead img (Riverside Library), not h2.section-title#mtitle (BIO 204 LMS). The mechanism is now an image-of-text whose glyph size must be measured (~15.75pt normal), NOT a 1.5rem heading shrunk by an 87.5% root font-size to 21px; color #888888 (3.54:1), not #838383 (3.79:1). Note this case now overlaps the picture-with-significant-other-content aspect. Same broad aspect (size → threshold), same expected=failed.

aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.mechanism: The card heading (.panel h2, #8c8c8c, font-size:14pt/weight 400 = 18.667px) qualifies for the relaxed 3:1 only when BOLD; at weight 400 it is normal text whose large-scale boundary is 18pt, and 14pt < 18pt, so 4.5:1 applies. Over the faint white→#efefef panel gradient the contrast is 3.36:1 (best) down to ~2.92:1 (worst), below 4.5:1, so it fails. The verdict turns on the weight-conditional large-scale rule.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.scenario: Glassroom workspace card heading (#8c8c8c, 14pt/weight 400) over a faint white-to-#efefef diagonal gradient; because 14pt is large-scale only when bold, this normal-weight heading needs 4.5:1 and at ~3.36:1 fails.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.note: Page was rewritten. primarySelector should be .panel h2 (Glassroom), not h2.course-head (Cantina del Molo). The mechanism is now 14pt normal-weight (large only if bold) over a gradient, NOT a condensed-face/font-stretch case; colors are #8c8c8c on a white→#efefef gradient, not #9c5a30 on #141414 (3.44:1). Same aspect (large-text classification), same expected=failed.

aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.mechanism: The refund-policy body (p.policy, #787878, 16px/weight 400 = 12pt normal, so 4.5:1 applies with no large-text relief) sits on a top-to-bottom white→#f4f4f4 'paper' gradient. The contrast is 4.4151:1 over the white top, dropping to ~4.0142:1 over the #f4f4f4 region — both below 4.5:1. The ratio is a normative threshold and must not be rounded up (4.4151:1 is not 4.5:1), so it fails.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.scenario: Fern & Field refund-policy page renders body text (#787878, 16px normal) over a white-to-#f4f4f4 paper gradient at 4.4151:1 (top) to ~4.0142:1 (bottom); the threshold is not rounded, so 4.4151:1 < 4.5:1 fails.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat.note: Page was rewritten. primarySelector should be p.policy (Fern & Field), not p.disclosure (Calverton DMV). The just-below-4.5 no-round mechanism is intact but the page is now over a white→#f4f4f4 gradient (4.4151:1→4.0142:1) rather than flat white; color #787878, not #767880 (4.40:1). Same aspect (hard 4.5:1, no rounding), same expected=failed.

state-dependent-text-contrast/case-01.mechanism: A meaningful in-scope placeholder (#tideline-postcode, stating the required postcode format) is painted pale grey #9aa0a6 over a CSS linear-gradient field fill, yielding ~2.48:1 at the light end down to ~1.53:1 at the deep-teal end — below 4.5:1 across the whole range. The 1.4.3 Understanding extends the SC to placeholder text, so this fails; a second faint placeholder (#tideline-promo) is decorative and excluded.
state-dependent-text-contrast/case-01.scenario: Tideline Sea-Swimming Club membership form: the empty postcode field shows a meaningful pale-grey placeholder (#9aa0a6) over a gradient fill at ~2.48→1.53:1, failing 1.4.3; typed dark values pass.
state-dependent-text-contrast/case-01.note: Page was rewritten. primarySelector should be #tideline-postcode::placeholder (Tideline swim-club form), not #q::placeholder (garden-centre catalogue). The failing placeholder is over a gradient fill (no single bg colour, ~2.48→1.53:1) with a decorative-placeholder carve-out, not flat white at 2.41:1; color #9aa0a6, not #a7a7a7. Same aspect (placeholder contrast), same expected=failed.

picture-with-significant-other-content-e.mechanism: The bistro's dinner menu is delivered as a single inline-SVG data-URI image, so the dish names and prices are image pixels, not live text. The graphic is a flat parchment fill plus menu lettering with no significant other visual content, so it is an in-scope image of text done for a custom hand-script look (exemption off). The rendered normal-size lettering is sepia #9c8e6f on parchment #f3ead7 = 2.70:1, below 4.5:1, so it fails.
picture-with-significant-other-content-e.scenario: Maison Verde bistro renders its dinner menu as a flat image-of-text (img.menu), sepia #9c8e6f on parchment #f3ead7 = 2.70:1 normal-size; in scope and below 4.5:1, so it fails.
picture-with-significant-other-content-e.note: Page was rewritten. primarySelector should be img.menu (Maison Verde bistro menu), not img#heroHeadingImg.headline (Cohere Ledger B2B SaaS hero). The in-scope flat-image-of-text contrast failure is intact, but the concrete instance differs: color pair #9c8e6f-on-#f3ead7 = 2.70:1, not warm-grey 3.25:1. Same aspect, same expected=failed.

decorative-vs-meaningful-text-exemption/.mechanism: Meaningful status text styled as a decorative overlay. The big platform code '.platform .code' (#c8cdca) is faded into an inline-SVG station-floorplan background-image as a 'map stamp', yet it is the ONLY place the rider's platform/track is named (the leg list has boarding group, car and fare but no platform). Because it is non-substitutable wayfinding information it is in scope, not pure decoration; eyedroppered over the pale floorplan tones it ranges ~1.4:1 down to ~1.1:1, and at 88px large-scale it fails even the relaxed 3:1 bar.
decorative-vs-meaningful-text-exemption/.scenario: Metra Transit ticket fades the big platform code 'B7' (#c8cdca) into a station-floorplan background-image as a decorative 'map stamp', but it is the sole platform cue on the ticket; over the pale floorplan it is ~1.4:1 down to ~1.1:1 and fails even the 3:1 large-text bar.

logotype-brand-exemption-and-erosion/cas.mechanism: The wordmark 'Mercato' is the page's SOLE home control: an SVG element with a rose-gold linearGradient fill, wrapped in with no separate 'Home' link and no logo . Because the logotype is acting as an interactive UI component, the 1.4.3 brand exemption is eroded and a sufficient-contrast variant is required but absent. The least-contrast pixel (lighter gradient stop #e0b483 on #ffffff) is ~1.91:1; at ~30px bold display it is large-scale, so even the relaxed 3:1 threshold governs and 1.91:1 fails it.
logotype-brand-exemption-and-erosion/cas.scenario: Mercato marketplace makes its rose-gold SVG-gradient wordmark (a.brand-home) the sole home link with no separate Home control or logo image, eroding the brand exemption; its least-contrast pixel ~1.91:1 fails even the 3:1 large-text bar.

logotype-brand-exemption-and-erosion/cas.mechanism: The home link <a class="brand" href="/wallet"> wraps TWO strings: the Arabic wordmark 'نسيج' (.mark, #6cbfb2 on white ~2.16:1) which IS the logotype and is exempt, and an appended descriptor 'الرئيسية' ('Home', .dest, #9aa7b0 on white ~2.46:1, 13px/weight 400). The descriptor is informative wayfinding text — brand-adjacent identity BEYOND the logo/logotype, which the exemption does not reach — so as normal-size text it must meet 4.5:1, and at ~2.46:1 it fails while the wordmark sibling is left exempt.
